question: Do the study's hotspots hold under a projected 2030s climate?

source.name: Climate DT (DestinE)
source.grid: HEALPix depth 7 (nside 128), NESTED, on a sphere

produced_by.download_and_conventions: healpix-convert ClimateDTConverter (GRID4EARTH, public on PyPI; byte-identical to the private legacy-converters)

sphere_to_wgs84.why: nearest is healpix-convert's declared resampler for these fields; its optional PSF correction is a deconvolution and drove 114 of 480 cells negative on precipitation, which a rate cannot be

produced_by.added_here: a month per request instead of a timestep, monthly aggregation, and the resampler restricted to the cells asked for
produced_by.sampling: 00 and 12 UTC each day; 240 months retrieved and discarded after aggregation

design.why_two_decades: a free-running projection cannot say what a given year was; comparing two decades of the same simulation isolates the climate change, not the weather
design.support: each depth-8 study cell inherits its depth-7 source cell (~51 km), twice its own width

verdict: unchanged: 95.51% (2020s) and 94.92% (2030s), both far outside the 47.8-68.6% reference range, so the Contradicted conclusion also holds under the projected climate
caveats: Climate DT SSP3-7.0 is served for 2020-2039 only (2018 and 2040 are refused), so the decades are 10 years apart and the forced signal is small (+0.14 degC) against internal variability
precipitation is estimated from the instantaneous rate at 00 and 12 UTC, not accumulated hourly totals; bio12 is 557-583 mm against 635 (ERA5) and 684 (CHELSA)
the support is a ~51 km source cell, twice the width of the study's cell
the -0.59 pp effect is of the same order as the 0.57 pp gap between our baseline and the published number
free-running projection: these years are plausible years, not observed ones (test 3 used ERA5 for the observed period)

healpix-convert's optional PSF correction was tried and rejected for this: being a deconvolution it drove 114 of 480 cells to negative precipitation and monthly totals as low as -193 mm, so the nearest resampler its settings declare is used instead
